title: Allow choosing the output folder / dataset name in preprocess.py
description: Output always goes to processed/<dataset>; output_folder is not exposed on the CLI. Only names in the datasets list or starting with 'TOL' are accepted, so e.g. 'nettraffic_day1' is skipped even though load_data would dispatch it. Currently worked around by renaming the output folder by hand.

title: Replace the TOL preprocessor with a TOL dataspec
description: Remove the separate TOL loader (and its --window, --top-k, --features options) in favor of a TOL dataspec JSON for the generic event-row processor (see issue 5). TOL data comes from a private source and will never be public, so the TOL spec is saved with the data, not committed to this repository. Check that the dataspec covers TOL's features (sent/received row counts, bytes/frame length, port entropy per IP) before removing tol.py.

title: General preprocessing method / common dataset format
description: Design. (1) Processed data format, the single contract between preprocessing and training/testing/reporting: a folder of .npy files, each a [timesteps, features] matrix, optionally with a segment-length list, and a label file for the test data. Any data in this form can be trained, tested and reported on. (2) Preprocessors: keep converters for common benchmark formats; the generic event-row processor (currently nettraffic with a dataspec JSON: a list of events with wide named columns, aggregated per interval) becomes the default preprocessing type. TOL folds into it and its separate preprocessor is removed. (3) Add a generic timestep-row processor: rows are already timesteps and columns are features (pandas or numpy input); it only splits and normalizes. (4) main.py: dataset is either the name of a folder in processed/ or a path to a folder with the required files.

title: ipykernel not declared in project dependencies
description: ipykernel was pip-installed into the AaltoAD env so VS Code can use it as a Jupyter kernel, but it is not in requirements.txt or pyproject.toml.

title: load_data reads global args for nettraffic options
description: The nettraffic branch of load_data uses args.port_entropy, args.bytes and args.temperature from the module-level args set in __main__, instead of function parameters. Calling load_data from anywhere else (imports, tests) raises NameError.

title: Fill in authors in pyproject.toml
description: Update authors in pyproject.toml to use local team names and revise later if needed. The authors list is currently empty. Moved from TODO.md, which also had a stray trailing line 'TranAD Contributors' (likely a leftover author entry).

title: Create a CITATIONS file
description: Create a CITATIONS file to document references and citations for the project. Moved from TODO.md.

title: Tests for --columns, timestamp detection and segment conversion
description: No tests cover parse_column_spec, find_timestamp_column raising when no candidate matches, or segment seconds->rows conversion (including the non-divisible error). The column rename and missing mapped column ValueError are covered in tests/test_preprocessing.py.

title: Move count-based metric calculations into the metrics module
description: Rates recomputed from summed confusion counts (no alarms involved) are implemented outside AaltoAD/metrics with different F1 conventions: thresholds.pooled._pooled_block (P/R/F1/fpr, zero-guard, keeps key case), report.metrics._pooled_f1 (exact 2tp/(2tp+fp+fn)), report.metrics.detected and detection_rate (alarm count/rate from upper-case POT counts only), the vectorised F1 in thresholds.oracle.shared_oracle_threshold (exact formula, now '>' via searchsorted side='right'), and utils.getresults2 (legacy TranAD helper, averages P/R then computes f1*; only used by tests/test_utils.py). Add a rates-from-counts function to the metrics module, which metrics.base._f1_from_predictions (epsilon 1e-5) can also use, and move these onto it. Alarm-based calculations (oracle_f1 final block, oracle_metrics, pot_fit.pot_metrics, merlin.get_result, pot.calc_seq, calc_point2point, thresholds.utils.prediction_metrics) are a separate step: replace them with metrics.common_metrics.

title: data_hash ignores segment lengths
description: data_hash hashes only train.npy. Changing only how the train data is split into segments leaves train.npy byte-identical, so a checkpoint trained with the old splits is reused. Include train_lengths.npy in the hash.

title: nettraffic processes columns by hardcoded name
description: _load_and_prepare still picks columns by name: the bytes column from a candidate list (bytes, length, len, ..., framelen) is converted to numeric with NaN -> 0, the temperature column (temperature or temp) to numeric, and temperature is set to NaN where a column named has_temp is false. Column names could be anything, and the dataspec features can use columns this does not touch (e.g. payload_len, n_msgs), which then rely on pandas' own type inference. Type handling (numeric conversion, fill, validity masks like has_temp) needs a place that does not depend on column names. Putting number types in the dataspec JSON seems like too much, but it has to be defined somewhere. Also: with has_temp present but no temperature column, the masking assigns to a column named None.

title: Move segments into the dataspec
description: Segments are given with --segment on the command line, and the same segments are applied to every CSV in a --csv group. Put them in the dataspec JSON instead, so the segmentation stays with the data definition.

title: Feature blocks for STAGNN and similar models
description: A feature block is a group_by value: every grouped feature gives one column per value, so each block has the same features in the same order (STAGNN's N x F node layout). Block construction was removed from the dataspec preprocessing for now; the columns are feature-major ({value}_{feature name}). Decide how blocks are built and marked, and wire them to the model calls. This applies to all GNN models (STAGNN, GDN, MTAD_GAT): they should receive features in packages, collected by the IP they relate to. Once supported, add it as an experiment variation (each GNN model with and without IP blocks).

title: Threshold method switches in the experiments JSON
description: This is about the experiments JSON files. run_experiment has run_oracle, run_pot and run_conformal keyword arguments (default True); nothing passes them yet (run_all, worker, experiments JSON). Related problems to fix with it: with run_pot=False or run_oracle=False the labels CSV code raises NameError (pot_pred, pot_expanded_pred, oracle_pred, oracle_expanded_pred are undefined); there is no conformal_label column in the labels CSV; append_benchmark_row writes no conformal columns; the report's shared.apply_blocks overwrites the runtime conformal blocks at the top level.

title: Tests for the dataspec preprocessing
description: Nothing covers the new nettraffic path: _cut_segments (anomaly clipping, skip segments, the end-of-CSV check), add_grouped_columns (ranking over train segments, 'other'), _aggregate_segment (aggregations incl. entropy, column 'any', fixed columns and zero fill) and the per-partition stacking of features, labels and lengths.

title: Stale docs after the dataspec change
description: The last sentence of load_nettraffic's docstring still describes the old features (top_K IPs, port entropy, mean temperature) and the interval parameter. The first line of _load_and_prepare's docstring overstates column detection. DATASPEC_STEPS.md marks only step 1 done. README.md and doc/DATA_FORMAT_GUIDE.md may still mention the removed --interval, --temperature, --bytes and --port-entropy options.

title: Split main.py and install entry points
description: Everything runs through main.py or preprocess.py, and main.py combines training and reporting. Split it into separate training and reporting commands, and make these and preprocessing console entry points installed with the library (pyproject.toml).
